method: Read source definitions and temperature rules at exact subject SHA. Treat inventory only as subject data, not oracle. Independently open journal full text, primary publisher abstracts and author repository copies. Compare number, operator, measured variable/location, exposure duration, sensitive stage and applicability against spec 3.3 and 5.3. Search snippets guided access attempts but were not sole proof. No test, full check or build was run. No profile edit or remote comment was made.
interpretation: unsupported means the accessed evidence does not support the complete encoded daily operational mapping under spec 5.3. It does not mean that the crop has no heat/frost response or that every cited numeric statement is false. Exact-mapping support cannot be supplied by an implementation limitation admitting a proxy.

limitations: Lethal temperature of cultivated potato foliage (Seppänen et al. 2001, range -2.5 to -3.0 °C; warmer endpoint used); the canopy is destroyed below -4 °C.

Uses screen air temperature from weather data, not canopy or plant tissue temperature.

limitations: Luo 2011 Table 2 gives 35 °C maximum temperature as the failure point during inflorescence production and floral initiation (Björkman & Pearson 1998).
The source exposure was about one week at 35 °C; shorter exposures produced little injury and longer ones were lethal, so a single day above 35 °C is a much milder event.
Placing floral initiation in the FAO-56 mid-season stage is a Gilir assumption; it can fall in the development stage, before the head is visible.
Uses screen air temperature from weather data, not canopy or plant tissue temperature.
